title: Microsoft Purview Sensitivity & Retention Labels — Implementation
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (enterprise Microsoft Purview implementation).

Microsoft Purview portal / Security & Compliance PowerShell / Graph authored at exact detail from Microsoft public docs; Purview features are heavily licensing-/plan-dependent (E5 / E5 Compliance; some preview) and the portal is evolving — availability + paths cited or flagged 'verify your licensing/tenant', never invented. Regulatory/records/legal determinations (retention schedules, file plans, legal holds, insider-risk case actions) deferred to compliance/records/privacy/legal — solutions give the technical method + evidence, not the determination; policies piloted in simulation/test before enforcement. Automation is PowerShell (S&C PowerShell / Graph); no secrets in code. No client names.
hook: Implement sensitivity and retention labels that actually protect and govern content
problem: Labels are how Purview classifies, protects, and governs content — but a bad taxonomy or careless auto-labeling breaks user trust fast. This solution implements sensitivity and retention labels end to end: a workable label taxonomy, sensitivity labels with protection (encryption, marking, access), publishing policies, auto-labeling (client and service-side), and retention labels + label policies with adaptive scopes — piloted in simulation before enforcement, so content is classified and governed without disrupting users.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — sensitivity vs retention labels, taxonomy design, protection options, publishing, client vs service-side auto-labeling, and adaptive scopes.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (E5/E5 Compliance for auto-labeling, roles, classification scheme, stakeholders).

Implementation Guide — design the taxonomy, build + publish sensitivity labels (protection/marking), configure auto-labeling in simulation first, build retention labels + policies with adaptive scopes, validate, then enforce — pilot-first, each label/policy named.

5 PowerShell scripts — Discovery, Configuration/Remediation, Validation, Reporting, and a scope/health helper — authentic Security & Compliance PowerShell / Graph automation (read-only or -WhatIf by default; no credentials in code).
Validation gates (labels published, auto-label simulated then enforced, retention applied) plus Best Practices; records determinations deferred to records/legal.
short: Implement sensitivity & retention labels — taxonomy, sensitivity labels with protection + publishing, auto-labeling (simulated first), and retention labels + policies with adaptive scopes — so content is classified and governed without disrupting users. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
